title: Scatter plot with strong downward linear trend: correlation coefficient near -0.8
vignette: Inflammatory biological markers are clinically useful in a number of different ways, one being the assessment of disease activity in conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). A new inflammatory marker is being investigated in patients with active SLE flares. When the blood level of the new marker (in mg/L) is plotted against the C-reactive protein (CRP) level (also in mg/L), the following plot is obtained: as CRP increases, the new marker's level steadily decreases, with the data points clustering tightly along a downward-sloping line. Based on the plot, the correlation coefficient between the 2 variables is closest to which of the following values?

clues.text: plotted against the C-reactive protein (CRP) level
clues.note: Two continuous variables plotted against each other are summarized by a correlation coefficient (r) describing the strength and direction of their linear association.

clues.text: as CRP increases, the new marker's level steadily decreases
clues.note: An inverse relationship (one variable falls as the other rises) means a NEGATIVE correlation (r < 0).

clues.text: clustering tightly along a downward-sloping line
clues.note: Little scatter around the line = a STRONG association, so |r| is close to 1; combined with the negative direction, r is near -0.8.

whatMatters: The correlation coefficient (r) ranges from -1 to +1 and captures the STRENGTH and DIRECTION of a linear association. The points fall as CRP rises (NEGATIVE) with little scatter (STRONG), so r is close to -1 - best matched by -0.8. Answer E.
strategy: Read direction, then strength. Downward trend -> negative r (rules out all positive values). Tight clustering along the line -> strong association -> |r| near 1, so -0.8 beats -0.2. Reject +0.8/+0.2 (wrong sign - the trend is negative), 0 (that's no association/random cloud), and -0.2 (too weak for such tight clustering).

eliminations.label: +0.8 - wrong sign (positive)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a strong POSITIVE correlation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the marker DECREASES as CRP increases, so the association is negative, not positive. ✅ Correct if: both variables rose together with tight clustering.

eliminations.label: +0.2 - wrong sign and too weak
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a weak POSITIVE correlation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the direction is negative and the association is strong (tight clustering), not weak-positive. ✅ Correct if: a faint upward trend with lots of scatter.

eliminations.label: 0 - implies no association
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: no linear correlation (random scatter). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the points show a clear downward linear pattern, so r is not 0. ✅ Correct if: a shapeless cloud with no trend.

eliminations.label: -0.2 - correct sign but too weak
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a weak NEGATIVE correlation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the direction is right, but tight clustering along the line indicates a STRONG association (|r| near 1), so -0.8 fits better than -0.2. ✅ Correct if: a negative trend with substantial scatter around the line.

reasoning: The marker falls as CRP rises -> negative correlation (r < 0)
Points cluster tightly along the line -> strong association (|r| near 1)
Negative and strong -> r closest to -0.8
mechanism: A CORRELATION COEFFICIENT (r) mathematically describes how well a straight 'line of best fit' matches the plotted data for two variables, capturing TWO features: DIRECTION (polarity) and STRENGTH. Its value ranges from -1 to +1. The SIGN gives direction: POSITIVE r means the variables move together (both increase), NEGATIVE r means they move oppositely (one increases as the other decreases). The MAGNITUDE gives strength: the closer |r| is to 1, the tighter the points hug the line (stronger linear association); r = 0 means no linear association (random scatter). Here the new marker DECREASES as CRP INCREASES (negative direction) with the points clustering tightly along a downward line (strong association), so r is close to -1 - best represented by -0.8. Note that r is NOT the slope: a data set can have r = +1 (perfect fit) with any positive slope value. The distractors are wrong in sign (+0.8, +0.2), imply no association (0), or are too weak for the tight clustering (-0.2).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biostat > correlation coefficient r: ranges -1 to +1; sign = direction, magnitude = strength; r=0 no linear association; r is not the slope; r^2 = coefficient of determination.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Downward trend = negative r; tight clustering = strong -> r near -0.8.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on correlation coefficient, positive vs negative correlation, strength vs slope, or line of best fit? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Positive values wrong sign; 0 = no association; -0.2 too weak for tight clustering.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Scatter plot (stem image): points slope downward (negative) with minimal scatter (strong) -> correlation coefficient closest to -0.8.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: negative + tightly clustered scatter = strong negative correlation (r near -0.8); r measures strength/direction, not slope.

Biostat > 0 = none; near +/-1 = strong; r is not slope.

memoryHook: Points sliding downhill in a tight line = strong + negative = r near -0.8; a fuzzy cloud would be 0, and uphill would be positive.
